motivation: The user keeps Peri and embedding normalization and tied weights, while explicitly allowing RMSNorm or LayerNorm and learned affine parameters. Establish what bounds survive those choices before selecting a future model.
objective: Prove scoped finite-epsilon LayerNorm and learned-diagonal-affine bounds, then compare existing CPU operations with independent high-precision local formulas. No training or architecture selection.

equations.layernorm: LN_eps(x)=RMS_eps(C(x)); population variance divides by d, not d-1.
equations.affine: gamma elementwise-multiplied by the normalized vector, plus beta. Gamma and beta are fixed when considering input sensitivity.
equations.gamma_bound: G>=0 and every abs(gamma_i)<=G. Unconstrained training does not provide a fixed uniform G or beta norm bound.

proof_targets: Centering is nonexpansive in Euclidean norm.
Positive-epsilon LayerNorm output norm is at most sqrt(d).
Positive-epsilon LayerNorm has input Lipschitz bound 1/sqrt(epsilon), matching the existing RMS bound.
LayerNorm is invariant to adding any scalar multiple of the all-ones vector, including finite epsilon.
A coordinatewise scale with abs(gamma_i)<=G has Euclidean operator bound G.
Affine RMS has output bound G*sqrt(d)+||beta|| and input Lipschitz bound G/sqrt(epsilon).
Affine LayerNorm has the same output and input Lipschitz bounds under the explicit parameter conditions.

numerical_grid.direction: Repeat [1,-1,-1,1] and truncate to d coordinates. The same vector is the fixed output cotangent. At width 1 its sole entry is 1, so centering removes all input.
numerical_grid.inputs_exact: zero is all zeros; constant_3 is all threes; balanced_a is a*direction; shifted_balanced_0.02 is 3+0.02*direction. Reference uses the actual represented input, not an ideal decimal amplitude.
numerical_grid.affine_exact: none has no affine parameters. nonuniform uses torch.linspace(-2,2,d) for gamma and torch.linspace(-0.25,0.25,d) for beta, in the tested dtype; both require gradients. RMS uses the existing repaired RMS then explicit elementwise affine. LayerNorm uses native F.layer_norm with these same parameters.
numerical_grid.reference: Python Decimal at 80 digits, from exact represented floating input/gamma/beta/cotangent. Compute population mean/variance, normalized output and analytic full input VJP plus gamma/beta VJPs. Do not call Torch autograd or either normalization implementation in the reference.
numerical_grid.checks: Compare complete output and input-gradient vectors for all cases; compare both affine-parameter gradients where present. Require finite actual/reference values and relative L2 error <=0.001. An identically zero reference requires exactly zero actual output/gradient.
numerical_grid.policy: Complete and retain every case, including numerical failures; do not weaken the threshold or infer convergence. This measures implementations, not which normalizer learns better. Do not fix a native operation or change model code within this comparison.

limits: Bounds are for real arithmetic with positive width and epsilon. They do not imply stable optimization, preserved information, earlier grokking or generalization.
The affine input bounds hold at fixed gamma/beta with the stated bounds. No uniform bound along unconstrained parameter training is inferred.
No Peri, embedding, tied-readout or benchmark source changes; no optimizer updates or new task scores; no initializer or normalizer selected.
Local CPU numerical failures, if any, concern the tested implementations. They do not refute the real-arithmetic norm bounds or prove the whole architecture unsuitable.
The old ten full-stack numerical failures and deferred Muon/repair studies remain unchanged. Capacity and usual-gain experiment order is preserved.
